headline: Council removed downtown floor area limits, set new planning fees, ended remote public comment, and approved $100,000 for warming shelters.
summary: The council voted to remove floor area ratio limits from the Downtown Development District. It approved up to $100,000 in block grant money for The Well and a warming shelter. It also ended remote public comment and found that a councilor violated two ethics code provisions, requiring training.
decisions: Approved the consent agenda, including a $12,931,640 airport security checkpoint contract and a $273,902 plow truck purchase.
Referred resolves 26-301 and 26-302 to committee and first reading.
Approved removing floor area ratio limits from the Downtown Development District, 8-0.
Approved resolve 26-294 accepting and appropriating $823,851 for the Nourish Maine nutrition education program.
Approved resolve 26-295 accepting and appropriating up to $6,000 from Johns Hopkins University for PrEP access.
Approved the special amusement permit for Benjamin's Restaurant and Pub, 123 Franklin Street, with no objections.
Approved the special amusement permit for Penobscot Theatre Company, 131 Main Street.
Approved ending public comment by remote means under the Remote Participation Policy, 6-2.
Approved new planning fees for abutter mailings and stormwater permits.
Approved amending order 26-305 to remove a $5,000 allocation to Manna Ministries, 7-0.
Approved order 26-305 as amended, providing up to $100,000 in block grant funds for The Well and a warming shelter, 7-0.
Approved order 26-306 finding that Councilor Wayne Mallar violated two ethics code provisions and requiring training, 5-2.
discussion: Members of the public and council discussed ending remote public comment. Supporters said remote comment helps people who cannot attend in person. Others said remote comments have disrupted meetings.

Speakers debated the block grant order for warming shelter and day space funding. Supporters said cold weather puts lives at risk. Others called the funding a temporary fix and asked for housing and prevention.
Speakers debated the causes of homelessness. Some pointed to addiction. Others pointed to housing costs, low wages, and disability.
Speakers spoke for and against the ethics order and its training requirement. One speaker asked that the ethics process be applied evenly. Another asked that all councilors take the training.
A council member asked for information on how block grant money will be spent before payments are issued.
